unit.title: The Sikh Panth Under Mughal Rule

contentBlocks.text: You've learned about early cooperation. Today: how this relationship grew more complicated over later decades!

As the Sikh Panth continued to grow throughout the 1600s, becoming a larger and more organized community with its own institutions and leadership, its relationship with later Mughal rulers grew more complex than the relative cooperation of Akbar's era — a genuinely significant historical shift that this course will explore in more depth in a future, dedicated unit, since it deserves careful, thorough treatment. For now, explain why a community growing larger and more organized might naturally lead to a more complicated relationship with the ruling government of the time, even without any specific conflict yet described.
You just recognized this relationship's real complexity! Tomorrow we'll see how the Sikh Panth responded by strengthening its own identity.

objectives: Understand that the Sikh Panth's relationship with Mughal rule grew more complex over time
Explain a general reason a growing, organized community might see a more complex relationship with government
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review this week's context and cooperation work.
2. Introduce the general idea that the relationship grew more complex over time, without detailing specific events.
3. Have the child explain the general growth-and-complexity reasoning.
4. Complete the worksheet.
5. Preview tomorrow's Sikh-identity-strengthening lesson.
differentiationTips: Struggling: use a simple analogy — a small club that grows into a large, well-organized group naturally starts interacting differently with school administration than it did as a handful of friends

Ready for more: ask the child what kinds of institutions (leadership structure, gathering places, shared practices) a growing community might develop, and why those might draw more attention from a ruling government

Deliberately kept general — the specific, historically significant events of this period (including real hardship the Panth faced) deserve a dedicated, carefully-sourced future unit rather than being compressed into a brief mention here
teacherGuide.answerKey: A growing, more organized community naturally becomes more visible and significant to a ruling government, since it now has real institutions, leadership, and a larger shared identity — a government that might not have paid much attention to a small, informal group often takes real notice once that group becomes large and organized enough to represent a genuine social and political presence.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses this course's Mughal-era thread, acknowledging real historical complexity while deliberately deferring specific sensitive events to a future, dedicated, more carefully sourced unit.

generationData.instructions: Answer each question about the changing Mughal-Sikh relationship.
